A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work despite the SSTP retitling, and their text, equations, tables and figures are readable. Neither contains an appendix. However, v2 Section 4.5 references additional backbone results in Supplementary Material that is absent from the supplied PDFs. The main papers support reliable comparison; those supplementary results cannot be assessed.

before.justification: V1 reports original Argoverse 1 experiments with HiVT-64, HiVT-128 and HPNet, including retention-rate comparisons, dense-scene evaluations and dataset-distribution analysis.

after.justification: V2 reports original Argoverse 1 and Argoverse 2 experiments, component ablations, sensitivity studies and timing measurements. These are distinct from the prior-work training times compiled in Table 1.

M1.justification: V1 scores squared differences between HiVT objective values and selects by maximizing gain. V2 instead constructs output-gradient/decoder-embedding features, scores their cosine similarities and minimizes the selection score (Equations 2–6). Algorithm 1 also revises dynamic budget allocation and replaces the separate Fixed/Balanced formulations with a balanced SSTP pipeline. These change the selection procedure substantially.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates only Argoverse 1. V2 adds actual Argoverse 2 evaluations, extending coverage to different driving scenarios and a five-second observation window with six-second forecasting, versus Argoverse 1's two-second observation and three-second forecast. Other datasets mentioned in background discussions do not establish additional SSTP evaluations.

E2.justification: V1's external selection comparator is random sampling. V2 Table 2 adds K-means Clustering and Herding against SSTP on Argoverse 1 across all three retained prediction models. Table 3 evaluates Random and Clustering on Argoverse 2. The nonrandom comparators substantially strengthen the competitive comparison.

E3.justification: V2 substantially expands the evaluation design: QCNet/DeMo configurations for Argoverse 2, alternative selection backbones, pretraining budgets of 0/5/8/10/15/64 epochs and partition intervals of 5/10/20 agents. It adds 60% retention and no longer displays v1's 1%, 2% and 5% tests. The six prediction modes and minADE/minFDE/MR metrics remain.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's retention, density and transfer analyses, v2 adds explicit partition-only and submodular-only controls (Table 5), pretraining sensitivity (Table 6), selection-backbone comparisons (Table 7), partition sensitivity (Table 8) and measured efficiency analysis. V1's detailed low-retention dense-scene curves and distribution-variance analysis are replaced by more limited density summaries.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, performance error bars or significance tests. V1's variance across scenario-category proportions describes dataset balance; it is not an estimate of uncertainty in model performance.

E6.justification: Numerous results are revised or newly reported. Full-data HiVT-64 changes from 0.692/1.047/0.104 for minADE/minFDE/MR in v1 Figure 2 to 0.695/1.037/0.109 in v2 Table 2, although v2 Table 5 retains the earlier values. V2 adds Argoverse 2, comparator, ablation and timing results. Changed methods and incompletely specified settings prevent interpreting cross-version score differences as controlled performance gains.

T1.justification: The central mathematical formulation changes substantially: v1 Equation 1's squared objective-value differences become explicitly defined gradient features and a cosine-kernel criterion in v2 Equations 2–6, with a different optimization direction. The budget-allocation rule is also mathematically revised. Neither version provides a theorem or proof establishing the claimed submodular properties.

C1.justification: V1 presents Fixed and Balanced coreset construction and claims state-of-the-art compression with approximately preserved performance. V2 redefines the contribution around gradient-based SSTP, explicitly claims one-time selection with substantial training-time savings, and emphasizes improvements over full-data training in dense scenes. The central half-data and scenario-balancing goals remain, but the proposed contribution and claimed benefits expand materially.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations of why balancing and informativeness must work jointly, why moderate pretraining can outperform a converged selector, and how partition intervals should adapt to dataset characteristics. It also explicitly identifies selection overhead and performance at very low retention as limitations. These extend v1's predominantly distribution-imbalance and coreset-transfer interpretation.

D1.justification: V1 provides a detailed training recipe, including AdamW, 64 epochs, batch size 32, learning rate, weight decay, dropout and scheduling. V2 largely replaces this with references to official protocols, reducing self-contained reproducibility information. It adds a code-availability statement and repository pointer, baseline-selection descriptions, and RTX 4090 selection/training timings. The repository's availability was not externally verified.

R1.justification: V2 adds a dedicated long-tail trajectory-prediction discussion, positioning scenario-level selection against feature-learning approaches including FEND, Hi-SCL and TRACT. It also expands coverage of recent forecasting and condensation methods while removing earlier references such as Dataset Quantization and the federated submodular-selection work. This materially revises research positioning, beyond reference renumbering.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and substantial portions of the remaining prose are rewritten around SSTP. Problem formulation moves inside Method; the experimental narrative is reorganized into main results, ablations, efficiency and generalizability, with explicit limitations. Terminology, contribution organization and author information also change.

P2.justification: V1's opening scene examples reappear in v2 Figure 2 with revised distribution plots, rather than being wholly new illustrations. V2 adds an opening performance/timing graphic and substantially restructures result displays: v1's twelve-panel density/retention figure and embedded tables give way to larger comparison tables, four retention plots and separate ablation tables. Typography and page layout also change extensively.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's weak comparative and diagnostic evidence: nonrandom selection baselines, a second benchmark and component controls test whether the method offers benefits beyond random sampling and density balancing alone. Sensitivity studies and measured selection costs further strengthen its practical assessment. These gains outweigh reduced implementation detail and reporting inconsistencies, including differing full-data HiVT values and HPNet training times of 268.8 hours in Figure 1 versus 307.2 hours in Section 4.4. Those issues still limit reproducibility and confidence in precise efficiency claims.
